chunks: Al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'A thousand strikes with the sword are lighter than dying on one's bed.' He said, 'In the cause of God.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اَللَّهِ: In the cause of God (referring to jihad or righteous striving)
key_terms.مَوْتٌ عَلَى فِرَاشٍ: Dying on one's bed (implies a comfortable, passive, or domestic death)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's saying 'A thousand strikes with the sword are lighter than dying on one's bed'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'heaviness' of dying on one's bed refers specifically to a death devoid of active striving in God's cause, contrasting the spiritual burden of passive comfort with the ease of martyrdom 'in the cause of God' (fi sabilillah). This hadith, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *jihad* not merely as physical combat but as a state of spiritual readiness, where active sacrifice is preferred over a life of ease without divine purpose. It highlights the theological distinction between a natural death and a 'death of negligence,' elevating the status of those who engage in the path of God even through the sword.
